metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Naomi, PA | Fayette County
metaDescription: Naomi, PA mineral owners in Fayette County: we buy interests directly, with careful research into old coal and gas deed history before any offer.
heroLead: Naomi is a small Fayette County patch community, the kind of place built originally to house coal miners, and the mineral history under it tends to be as layered as the town's own past.
intro: Coal patch towns like Naomi were often built by coal companies that owned the mineral rights outright, at least at first, which means figuring out what your family actually retained or later acquired takes real research into old company records and county deeds together.
We buy mineral and royalty interests around Naomi directly. We do that historical digging ourselves and lay out exactly what we find before discussing any number with you.

sections.heading: A Coal Patch's Mineral History
paragraphs: Fayette County's coal patch communities, Naomi included, were frequently built on land where the coal company controlled both surface and subsurface rights initially. Over the following decades, as companies sold off holdings, oil and gas rights sometimes ended up with individual families while coal rights went a different direction entirely, or vice versa.
The Marcellus formation sits far below the coal seams that built this community, and operators have leased and developed acreage in this part of Fayette County over the past decade or more.

sections.heading: Untangling Old Company Records
paragraphs: We research your chain of title through the Fayette County Recorder of Deeds in Uniontown, working through old coal company conveyances where necessary to establish exactly how your family's interest came to exist.
This kind of research takes patience in patch-town areas, but it's necessary to give you a confident, accurate picture.

sections.heading: What We'll Explain Before Any Offer
paragraphs: We'll walk through what the title research shows, your current division order if one exists, and any royalty history available, so you understand your interest fully before a number comes up.

faqs.question: Did the coal company that built Naomi also own the gas rights?
faqs.answer: It varies by tract and by which company held the land. We research the specific chain of title for your parcel rather than assuming a blanket answer.

faqs.question: My family doesn't have much paperwork on this interest. Can you still help?
faqs.answer: Yes. We do most of the historical research ourselves through county and, where needed, company records, so incomplete family paperwork isn't a dead end.

faqs.question: Is there active drilling near Naomi right now?
faqs.answer: We check current activity specific to your parcel's unit as part of our review, since it varies across Fayette County's coal patch communities.
